Abbott et al. obtain
$-3\times10^{-15}\le\Delta c/c\le+7\times10^{-16}$ using a
conservative source distance, simultaneous emission for the upper
bound and a delayed gamma-ray emission assumption for the lower
bound~\cite[Sec.~4.1, Eq.~(1)]{Abbott2017GW170817}.
We adopt the symmetric envelope $|\Delta c/c|\le\tau$, with
$\tau=3\times10^{-15}$; alternative source-emission histories can
weaken this inferred propagation constraint. For the assumed law,
$\Delta c/c=\sqrt{\chi_{\mathrm{vest}}}-1$ when $c\ne0$.
The theorem
\leanref{GravitationalWaves.c_GW_match_iff_chi_close_to_one}
gives, for $\chi_{\mathrm{vest}}\ge0$,
\[
 |\sqrt{\chi_{\mathrm{vest}}}-1|\le\tau
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \chi_{\mathrm{vest}}\in[(1-\tau)^2,(1+\tau)^2].
\]
The comparison window $[0.1,10]$ is adopted about the exactly luminal
anchor $\chi_{\mathrm{vest}}=1$. Its physical normalization, center
and endpoints are not determined by the RPA resummation with
unevaluated bare-response and coupling inputs.
Both endpoints fail the cap
(\texttt{natural\_endpoints\_violate\_ligo\_window}), while the
compatible interval lies strictly inside the comparison window and
contains unity
(\texttt{ligo\_confines\_chi\_vest\_within\_natural\_range} and
\texttt{chi\_one\_mem\_ligo\_window}).
Its width is exactly $4\tau$ and is smaller than the comparison-window
width by more than fourteen orders of magnitude
(\texttt{ligo\_window\_width\_eq} and
\leanref{ligo_window_width_lt_natural_range_width_by_1e14}).
This width comparison assigns no probability without a prior.
The susceptibility offsets are $-2\tau+\tau^2$ and
$2\tau+\tau^2$; $\tau$ bounds the speed deviation.
